thread:
sara: dropping a follow-up from the rate-limiter shard design sesh. want to capture a few edge tradeoffs we didn't finalize.

oliver: nice. the biggest open for me is spillover semantics. do we let a tenant consume spare capacity on other shards in-band or force migration?

marta: in-band spill is simpler for low-latency bursts, but it breaks local fairness guarantees. alternative: short-lived spill tokens that are issued by donors and expire quickly.

kevin: spill tokens sound promising. implementation thought: donor shard issues a signed token containing bucket id + expiry + nonce. recipient shard validates signature and debits. cheap and stateless.

sara: that reduces cross-shard state, good. but we still need a way to know which shards have spare capacity. polling everyone is expensive.

oliver: advertise summaries using compact sketches (e.g., reservoir sketches or tiny histograms) every 500ms. recipients can check approximate free-capacity without heavy exchange.

marta: yes — sketch advert + TTL. estimator error is fine; we'll tune the sketch size so false-negatives are rare. the rebalancer can be conservative to avoid oscillation.

kevin: question: how do we keep abuse signals consistent? if one shard flags a tenant as abusive, others need to respect that quickly.

sara: propose a write-through abuse ledger: shards append abuse events to a centralized append-only store. shards read the latest pointer periodically (cache with 1-2s ttl). critical blocks (e.g., temporary ban) should be pushed via push-notify channel to reduce window.

oliver: append-only store could be backed by existing event-log infra, great for audit too. we should define idempotent event types: score-update, probation-start, probation-end.

marta: another nuance: multi-dim quotas (tokens, embeddings, realtime concurrency). keep tenant->shard mapping by tenant so accounting is co-located, but per-dimension enforcement within-shard follows orthogonal counters. global enforcement (sum across shards) uses periodic aggregate snapshots + a slow-path check on thresholds.

kevin: slow-path check needs to be rare. target: 99.95% fast pass local-only. if aggregate snapshot is stale and threshold crossed, we can revoke provisional admits retroactively (with TTL) rather than blocking immediately.

sara: revocation with TTL works operationally if we accept small transient overages. for strict billing/legal quotas we must fail closed — in those cases the shard should consult a strong central authority on each request (documented as a slow path).

oliver: rollout plan idea: feature-flag staged rollout by tenant size class. start with tiny tenants (no critical SLAs), then medium, then big. measure provisional token issuance rate and cross-shard traffic.

marta: also simulation: reproduce skewed hotspot patterns (10% tenants create 80% load) and verify rebalancer damping factor. need hysteresis and cooldown per-tenant to stop ping-pong.

kevin: lease semantics: maintain a short lease with generation counter per-tenant in metadata store. when migrating, acquire lease with CAS. if two shards race we'll pick the higher generation; losers backoff. avoids hard consensus.

sara: important: leases must be namespaced by region/cluster so we don't move tenants between incompatible zones accidentally. and all APIs require mTLS auth.

oliver: ops playbook: if we detect oscillation (migrations/sec > threshold), flip to local-only mode and increase provisional expiry to flatten load. create an alert that automatically pauses the rebalancer.

marta: monitoring: migration rate, token spill rate, per-tenant cooldown violations, sketch-estimation-error, abuse-event lag. add synthetic canary that blasts one tenant to ensure protections kick in.

kevin: security note: adverts carry only capacity sketches and no tenant-identifying data except shard-id. token issuance requires shard identity proof and signed keys rotated daily.

sara: next steps: oliver will draft advert proto and sketch size recommendations. marta will author the migration lease spec. kevin will prototype signed spill-token format. i'll open follow-up tickets and a canary simulation job.

ops-bot: created INFRA-1701 "spill-token + sketch adverts + migration lease follow-ups" and linked this thread.

oliver: thanks all. let's sync in infra-arch next Tuesday.

marta: i'll post a short design doc with diagrams before then.

kevin: assigning myself to the token prototype.

sara: great, talk soon. :rocket:
